subject: general
question: Which crop variety improvement method involves selecting parents with desirable traits and crossing them?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hybridisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hybridisation** is a traditional method of **crop variety improvement** that involves the **crossing** of two or more plants with different **genotypes** to produce a new variety.
 
• The goal of this process is to combine **desirable phenotypic traits**—such as **high yield**, **disease resistance**, and **nutritional quality**—found in different parent plants into a single **hybrid** progeny.
 
• This method can be categorized based on the relationship between parents: **Intervarietal** (between two different **varieties**), **Interspecific** (between two different **species** of the same **genus**), and **Intergeneric** (between two different **genera**).
 
• The mechanical process of hybridisation involves several critical steps: **selection of parents**, **emasculation** (the removal of stamens to prevent self-pollination), **bagging** to prevent contamination, and **artificial cross-pollination**.
 
• By creating new **genetic combinations**, hybridisation has been a cornerstone of the **Green Revolution**, leading to the development of **high-yielding varieties (HYV)** of crops like **wheat** and **rice**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Hybridisation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tissue Culture:**
 
 
• This is an **in vitro** technique where **cells, tissues, or organs** are grown in a **synthetic nutrient medium** under **aseptic conditions**.
 
• It allows for the rapid **cloning** of plants, known as **micropropagation**, and is used to produce **disease-free** plants from **meristems**.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Engineering:**
 
 
• This modern **biotechnology** involves the **direct manipulation** of an organism's **DNA** to introduce a specific **foreign gene** (transgene).
 
• It results in **Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs)**, such as **Bt Cotton**, which possesses **insecticidal properties** derived from the bacterium **Bacillus thuringiensis**.
 
 
 
• **Mutation Breeding:**
 
 
• This method utilizes **physical mutagens** (like **gamma rays** or **X-rays**) or **chemical mutagens** to induce sudden, **heritable changes** in the plant's **genetic sequence**.
 
• It is used to create **genetic variation** when the desired trait is not available in the existing **germplasm** of the crop.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection**: Before crossing, breeders perform **mass selection** or **pure-line selection** to ensure the **parental plants** are of the highest quality and possess the specific **traits** required for the improvement program.
 
• **Heterosis**: Also known as **hybrid vigor**, this is the phenomenon where the **hybrid offspring** exhibits superior **biological functions** (like faster growth or higher yield) compared to either of its **parents**.
 
• **Objectives of Crop Improvement**: Scientists focus on **biotic resistance** (against pests and pathogens), **abiotic resistance** (against **drought**, **salinity**, and **heat**), and **shorter maturity duration** to allow farmers to grow multiple **crops** in a **year**.
